To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
specific glycoproteids are differentially distributed among the various regions of a single neuron.
the carbohydrate moities of a single glycoprotein extend from the surface of R2's cell membrane and that the carbohydrate of another glycoprotein is located in the axon.

glycoproteins of the surface membrane of R2's cell soma differ in their distribution from those of the axon, that the carbohydrate moeities of at least one of the glycoproteins (glycoprotein-I) extend from the surface, and that the glycoproteic content of R2's external membrane can be altered by treatment with proteases in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of specific macromolecules among the regions of the cell.
the molecular mechanisms that control the distribution of macromolecules within cells.
the distribution and metabolism of specific glycoprotein in the various compartments of R2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distribution of specific membrane glycoprotein is different in the cell body and the axon.
the surface membrane of R2 contains a glycoprotein that is enriched in fucose, N-acetylgalacotosamine, and galactose and that is absent from the axonal membranes.
glycoprotein-V is found predominantly in the axon, glycoprotein-I is enriched in the external membrane and glycoprotein-VIII is found in the internal membranes of the soma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the distribution of specific membrane glycoprotein is determined by the site in the neuron at which the carbohydrate chains are assembled and/or by the differential removal of the carbohydrate moieties at particular sites in the neuron.
glycoprotein-V is localized in the axon and glycoprotein-I is localized in the cell body and its surface membrane.
specific glycoproteines are routed to different regions of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of specific proteins and glycoproteins in R2 can be determined and that the cell body and axon are distinct with respect to their macromolecular compositions.
the glycoproteins of the surface membrane and axon differ in composition, and this is reflected in the distribution of the labeled glycopeptides released by pronase treatment of R2.
the surface of R2 is composed of several glycoproteins that are differentially distributed among the various regions of the cell.
